sections.title: Sound of ene
paragraphs: The letter name is (ene) /ˈene/. Its main sound is heard in the word (noche) /ˈno.t͡ʃe/, which means night. This consonant has four sounds in speech. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Let the air pass out through your nose, with your vocal cords vibrating. Next, close your lips completely to let the sound flow out through your nose. Then, raise the back of your tongue against the soft roof. Finally, press the flat middle part of your tongue against the hard roof. Put a hand on your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: Before a vowel or at the start of a word, it makes the sound in (noche) /ˈno.t͡ʃe/. Before bilabial consonants, it changes to the sound in (un beso) /um ˈbe.so/. Before velar consonants, it becomes the back sound in (cinco) /ˈθiŋ.ko/. Before palatal sounds, it makes the sound in (ancho) /ˈaɲ.t͡ʃo/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not hold the tongue on the tooth ridge before every consonant. In words like song, the nasal sound moves to the back. A nasal is a sound where the air goes out through the nose. Let your mouth adapt to the next consonant smoothly.
